mainTopic: The holiness of a בית כנסת and בית מדרש, eulogizing Torah scholars, and the honor due to those who learn הלכות
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא about what may and may not be done in a בית כנסת. Personal uses such as grooming, strolling, taking shelter from sun or rain, and a private הספד are forbidden. Torah reading, learning and a public הספד are allowed. רבי יהודה adds that a ruined בית כנסת is left with its grass as a sad reminder to rebuild, and the גמרא fills in a missing line about sweeping the floor. רב אסי teaches that the synagogues of בבל are built with a תנאי, but business calculations there are still forbidden and bring punishment. The גמרא then explains the ברייתא's clauses: scholars may treat the study hall like home, a person may enter for learning even when it rains, and someone who must call a friend out should first say some Torah. It defines a public הספד as one the whole community attends, and contrasts ריש לקיש's warm eulogy of a back-row scholar with רב נחמן's refusal to eulogize a man who was not proficient. It closes with teachings on not being served by Torah learners and on the reward for learning הלכות, and then opens a new ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Personal-use activities forbidden in a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its list of forbidden uses: no grooming, no strolling, no using the בית כנסת as shelter from sun or rain, and no private הספד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not adorn oneself in them, and one may not stroll in them, and one may not enter them in the heat to escape the heat, or in the rain to escape the rain. And one may not give a eulogy in them for an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting a ברייתא that lists things you may NOT do in a בית כנסת. All of these treat the building like a private convenience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The common thread is personal benefit. Grooming, strolling, or ducking in to escape the weather uses the holy building for your own comfort. A הספד for an ordinary individual is a private family event, so it also does not belong there.

keyTerms.meaning: Making oneself look nice or getting personal benefit (from נאה, 'pleasant')
Strolling or walking around for pleasure
In the heat or the sun
A eulogy for an individual, a private mourning event

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a ברייתא. The opening of the list (no קלות ראש, no eating or drinking, and so on) came on the previous amud, so the 'וְ' ('and') at the beginning continues that earlier list.

phrases.english: And one may not adorn oneself (or take personal benefit) in them,
and one may not stroll about in them,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין נִכְנָסִין בָּהֶן בַּחַמָּה מִפְּנֵי הַחַמָּה,
phrases.english: and one may not enter them in the heat to escape the heat,
or in the rain to escape the rain.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַסְפִּידִין בָּהֶן הֶסְפֵּד שֶׁל יָחִיד.
phrases.english: And one may not give a eulogy in them for an individual.
phrases.notes: A private eulogy that does not involve the whole community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Personal-convenience uses of a בית כנסת and a private הספד are forbidden.

steps.title: Activities permitted in a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists what IS allowed: reading Torah, learning, and a public הספד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may read Scripture in them, and learn in them, and give a eulogy in them for the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now turns from forbidden uses to permitted ones. Holy and communal activities are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading and learning Torah fit the holy purpose of the building. A הספד that involves the whole community, for example for a תלמיד חכם, is a public matter and is allowed. This contrasts with the private הספד forbidden in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning, meaning studying משנה and הלכה
A eulogy for the public, attended by the community

steps.whatToRemember: The dividing line is private benefit (forbidden) versus holy or communal use (permitted).

phrases.english: But one may read Scripture in them, and learn in them,
and one may give a eulogy in them for the public,
phrases.notes: For example, for a Torah scholar whose הספד the community attends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the permitted side, in contrast to the forbidden list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah reading, Torah learning, and a public הספד are permitted in a בית כנסת.

steps.title: A ruined synagogue is left to grow grass
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says these rules apply while the בית כנסת is in use. A ruined one is left alone, and the grass that grows there is not pulled, because of עגמת נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? When they are inhabited. But when they are in ruins, they are left alone and grass grows in them, and one should not pick it, because of the anguish it causes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a rule about a בית כנסת that has fallen into ruin. Notice that he talks about grass, which the ברייתא never mentioned. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the grass makes people sad when they see it, and that sadness pushes them to rebuild. Pulling it out would hide the ruin.

keyTerms.meaning: While they are inhabited, in active use
Anguish or distress of the soul

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When does this apply? When they are inhabited,
but when they are in ruins, they are left alone
and grass grows up in them,
and one should not pull it out, because of the anguish it causes.
phrases.notes: Seeing the grass causes distress that pushes people to rebuild.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit and a special rule to the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ruined בית כנסת is left alone, and grass that grows in it is not removed.

steps.title: Who said anything about grass?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה talks about grass when the ברייתא never mentioned it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grass — who mentioned it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem. רבי יהודה seems to be reacting to something about grass, but nothing in the ברייתא discusses grass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אֵימָתַי', 'when does this apply', means רבי יהודה is limiting an earlier rule. Yet his limit is about grass, and no earlier rule addressed grass. So the text as we have it does not hold together.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned their name? (Nobody brought this up!)

phrases.english: Grass — who mentioned it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A limiting clause ('when does this apply') must refer to an earlier rule, but no earlier rule discussed grass.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing a line about sweeping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is missing a line: the floors of a בית כנסת are swept and sprinkled so grass does not grow. It then repeats רבי יהודה's statement in its corrected form.
steps.simpleTranslation: The text is missing something, and this is what it teaches: And one sweeps them and sprinkles water on them so that grass will not grow in them. רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? When they are inhabited, but when they are in ruins, they are left for grass to grow. If grass grew in them, one should not pull it, because of the anguish it causes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the missing line of the ברייתא so that רבי יהודה's comment makes sense. It then restates רבי יהודה's words on purpose, inside the corrected text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the added rule about sweeping 'so grass will not grow', רבי יהודה's 'when does this apply' now has something to limit. Sweeping is only needed in a working בית כנסת, and a ruined one is left so grass grows. The repetition here is not redundant: it shows how the full ברייתא really reads.

keyTerms.meaning: It is missing something (the text has a gap)
And this is what it teaches
Sprinkling water on the floor to keep down dust

steps.confusionAlert: חסורי מיחסרא does not mean the rabbis disagree with the ברייתא. It means the wording is shortened, and the גמרא is filling in the missing words.
steps.whatToRemember: A working בית כנסת is kept clean so grass does not grow. A ruined one is left with its grass as a sad reminder to rebuild.

phrases.english: The text is incomplete, and this is what it teaches:
And one sweeps them and sprinkles water on them
so that grass will not grow in them.
Rabbi Yehuda said: When does this apply? When they are inhabited,
but when they are in ruins, they are left for grass to grow.
If grass grew in them, one should not pull it out,
because of the anguish it causes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 4 by adding the missing line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's mention of grass seemed to have no anchor in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא includes a rule to sweep and sprinkle so grass does not grow, and רבי יהודה limits that rule to a working בית כנסת.

steps.title: Babylonian synagogues are built with a condition
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי teaches that the synagogues of בבל are built with a תנאי, which allows some other uses, yet קלות ראש is still forbidden in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: The synagogues in בבל are built on condition. And even so, one may not act with frivolity in them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב אסי says the synagogues of בבל were built from the start with a condition that loosens some of the strict rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the תנאי, the community may use these buildings for some general needs. The building is still a בית כנסת, and the תנאי only changes how some rules apply. That is why קלות ראש remains forbidden even there.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition, a stipulation made when the building was built

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the idea that a תנאי can relax some uses of a בית כנסת, but basic respect for the place always remains.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת שֶׁבְּבָבֶל, עַל תְּנַאי הֵן עֲשׂוּיִין.
phrases.english: The synagogues in Babylonia are built on condition.
phrases.notes: Built on condition that they may be used for some community needs.

phrases.english: And even so,
one may not act with frivolity in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת שֶׁבְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אמורא statement that limits how strictly the ברייתא's rules apply in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Babylonian synagogues are built with a תנאי, yet קלות ראש is still forbidden in them.

steps.title: What counts as frivolity: business calculations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what קלות ראש means here and answers: doing business calculations (חשבונות).
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is that? Calculations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of קלות ראש is still forbidden even with the תנאי, and gives a short answer: business calculations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תנאי already allows some general uses, the גמרא needs to say what remains forbidden. Doing business accounts treats the holy space as an office, so it counts as קלות ראש.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is it? (asking for a definition)
Calculations or accounts, meaning business reckoning

steps.whatToRemember: Even with a תנאי, a בית כנסת may not be used for business calculations.

phrases.english: And what is that? Business calculations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term קלות ראש used by רב אסי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What specific behavior counts as קלות ראש in a synagogue built with a תנאי?

steps.title: Calculations in a synagogue lead to a corpse being kept there overnight
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי warns that a בית כנסת where people do business calculations will end up holding a dead body overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: In a בית כנסת where people do business calculations, they will keep a dead body overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives a sharp warning about what happens to a בית כנסת where people do business accounts. The warning is that a dead body will end up being kept there overnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues from Step 7, where קלות ראש was defined as doing חשבונות. רב אסי now attaches a consequence to it. Taken literally, his words sound like an instruction, as if people should keep a corpse there. That odd wording is exactly what the גמרא questions next.

keyTerms.meaning: They keep overnight (from לָן, to stay the night)

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
A synagogue in which they make business calculations —
they keep the corpse inside it overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definition of קלות ראש as חשבונות and states what happens as a result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing business calculations in a בית כנסת leads to a corpse being kept there overnight.

steps.title: Can it really mean they will keep a corpse there?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: surely there is always some other place to keep a body, so why would anyone keep it in a בית כנסת?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They keep a corpse overnight' — can you really think that? Is there no other option?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי's wording. It is hard to believe that people would actually have to keep a body in a בית כנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a body is cared for by family and taken elsewhere. There is always some other choice. So the plain reading of רב אסי does not make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? (signals that the reading being suggested is impossible)
Is it not possible? / Is there no way?

phrases.english: "They keep overnight" — can that enter your mind?
Is there no other way besides this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal wording of רב אסי's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's words 'מלינין בו את המת'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is always somewhere else to keep a body, so it makes no sense that people would be forced to keep it in a בית כנסת.

steps.title: It means they will end up keeping a מת מצוה there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that as a punishment, people will die, including someone with no one to bury him. In the end, that מת מצוה will be kept in the בית כנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, in the end they will have to keep a מת מצוה there overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב אסי was describing a punishment, not giving an instruction. People will die, and eventually an abandoned body will have to stay in the בית כנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading changes 'מלינין' (they keep) into 'לסוף שילינו' (in the end they will keep). A מת מצוה has no family to take care of it, so it really may have nowhere else to go. That answers the challenge in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead person with no one to bury him, whom everyone is obligated to bury

steps.confusionAlert: רב אסי is not allowing anyone to keep a body in a בית כנסת. He is describing a punishment: disrespect for the בית כנסת brings death to the community.

phrases.english: Rather, in the end they will keep inside it overnight
a corpse with no one to bury it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְסוֹף שֶׁיָּלִינוּ בּוֹ מֵת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by re-reading רב אסי's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording: the statement describes a future punishment, not a present practice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי meant that people actually keep a body in the בית כנסת, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the sin, deaths will come, and eventually a מת מצוה will have to be kept there.

steps.title: Sages and their students may make personal use of the study hall
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא said one may not adorn oneself in a בית כנסת. רבא says חכמים and their students are allowed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'And one may not adorn oneself in them.' רבא said: Sages and their students are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves on to the next line of the ברייתא, the ban on adorning oneself there. רבא limits that ban by saying it does not apply to חכמים and their students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's rule seemed to cover everyone. רבא carves out an exception for Torah scholars. The reason for this exception comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Adorn oneself or enjoy personal benefit (from נָאֶה, pleasant)

phrases.english: And one may not adorn oneself inside them.
Rava said:
Sages and their students are permitted,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on making personal use of a בית כנסת does not apply to חכמים and their students.

steps.title: The study hall is the 'house' of the Sages
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that 'בי רבנן' means 'ביתא דרבנן', the Sages' home. So scholars may treat it like their home.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What does 'בי רבנן' mean? 'ביתא דרבנן', the house of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבא's ruling from Step 11. It uses רבי יהושע בן לוי's explanation of the name of the study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בי' is a shortened form of 'ביתא', meaning home. If the study hall is the Sages' home, they may use it the way a person uses his own house. This lets them stay there and learn all the time.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall (literally 'the בי of the Sages')

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that Torah scholars may eat, drink, and rest in a בית מדרש.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
What is the meaning of "bei of the Sages" —
the house of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and source for רבא's exception.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that scholars may use the study hall for personal needs
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of 'בי רבנן' as 'ביתא דרבנן'

steps.title: Do not enter a synagogue just for shelter from sun or rain
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's next line says one may not go into a בית כנסת just to get out of the sun or the rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not enter them in the sun because of the sun, or in the rain because of the rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. This sets up the story that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a בית כנסת only as shelter treats it like an ordinary building. The rule targets entering for that reason alone. The story will show that the same act is fine when done for a proper purpose.

phrases.english: And one may not enter them
in the sun because of the sun
or in the rain because of the rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין נִכְנָסִין בָּהֶן בַּחַמָּה מִפְּנֵי הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to enter a בית כנסת just for shelter from sun or rain.

steps.title: The Sages who entered during rain for the sake of learning
steps.stepSummary: רבינא and רב אדא בר מתנה were asking רבא a question when rain began. They went into a בית כנסת and said they were entering because learning needs clear thinking, not because of the rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רבינא and רב אדא בר מתנה. They were standing and asking רבא a question when a shower of rain came. They went into the בית כנסת and said: 'We are not entering because of the rain. We are entering because a הלכה needs clarity, like a clear day with a north wind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the rule from Step 13 in action. It also shows how to enter properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages did get out of the rain, but their stated purpose was Torah study. Entering a בית כנסת to learn is allowed. So what matters is the reason you enter, and protection from the rain was only a side effect.

keyTerms.meaning: North wind (which brings a clear sky)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרָבִינָא וְרַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה
phrases.english: Like that case of Ravina and Rav Adda bar Mattana
who were standing and asking a question of Rava,
when a shower of rain came;
they entered the synagogue
and said: This that we entered the synagogue
is not because of the rain,
but because a halakhic discussion requires clarity
like a day of the north wind.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרָבִינָא וְרַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the ברייתא's rule with a real case and shows the proper way to enter.
steps.raayaObject: The rule against entering a בית כנסת only for shelter
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבינא and רב אדא בר מתנה with רבא
steps.whatToRemember: Your reason for entering a בית כנסת matters. Going in only for shelter is forbidden, but going in for Torah study is allowed, even if it also keeps you dry.

steps.title: How may one enter a synagogue to call someone out?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי what to do if you need to call a person out of a בית כנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: If a person needs to call someone out of a בית כנסת, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: A practical question is raised. Going in only to call someone seems like using the בית כנסת for a personal need, so how can a person do it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that a proper purpose permits entering. This question asks how to supply such a purpose when your real reason is only to fetch someone.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
If a person needs
to call a man from the synagogue, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea of 'entering for a proper purpose' to a new practical case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a person can properly enter a בית כנסת when his real reason is to call someone out.

steps.title: Say some Torah, have a child say a verse, or sit a little
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the person should say Torah at his own level: a הלכה, a משנה, or a פסוק. If he cannot, he should ask a child to say a verse, or else sit for a short while before leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If he is a young scholar, he should say a הלכה. If he is a תנא, he should say a משנה. If he knows תנ״ך, he should say a פסוק. If not, he should say to a child: 'Tell me your verse.' Or else, he should wait a little and then get up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives practical ways to turn entering the בית כנסת into a proper visit. Each option fits a different level of learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each option adds a holy purpose to the visit: learning, hearing Torah, or simply sitting there. Sitting a little shows the person did not come in only for a personal errand. Even someone who cannot learn has a way to do it properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who has memorized many משניות and ברייתות

steps.whatToRemember: To enter a בית כנסת for a personal need, give the visit a proper purpose. Say some Torah, hear a child's פסוק, or sit for a bit before leaving.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן הוּא —
phrases.english: He said to him: If he is a young Torah scholar —
let him say a halakha;
and if he is a tanna — let him say a mishna;
and if he is a Bible expert — let him say a verse.
And if not, let him say to a child:
Tell me your verse.
Alternatively, let him wait a little and then get up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Give the visit a holy purpose by saying a הלכה, a משנה, or a פסוק according to your level. Otherwise, have a child recite a verse or sit briefly before leaving.

steps.title: A public eulogy may be held in a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one may hold a הספד של רבים, a public eulogy, inside a בית כנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may eulogize in them a eulogy of the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא about how to treat a בית כנסת. It quotes the next allowed use: a public eulogy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier lines listed things you may NOT do in a בית כנסת, such as entering only to escape the sun or rain. This line gives a permitted use. A eulogy for the community is a public, respectful event, so it fits the dignity of the building.

keyTerms.meaning: A eulogy for someone who died

phrases.english: And one may eulogize in them (synagogues)
a eulogy of the public.
phrases.notes: A eulogy that many people attend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא after the side discussion about calling someone out of a בית כנסת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public eulogy may be held inside a בית כנסת.

steps.title: What counts as a public eulogy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of a הספד של רבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a public eulogy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly makes a eulogy count as public. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allowed only a public eulogy, so we need to know where the line is. Is it about who died, or about how many people come? The answer will define the case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of a public eulogy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact circumstances that make a eulogy count as 'public'.

steps.title: Each Sage humbly points to the other
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says: a eulogy that רב ששת attends. רב ששת says: a eulogy that רב חסדא attends.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא illustrated: For example, a eulogy at which רב ששת is present. רב ששת illustrated: For example, a eulogy at which רב חסדא is present.
steps.whatsHappening: Two Sages answer the question with an example. A eulogy is public when a great Sage attends, because then the whole community comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the rule: a great Sage's presence draws the public. Each one humbly names the other as the great Sage instead of himself. So the definition is about how many people come, which depends on who attends.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he stands, is present at it

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא and רב ששת are not arguing. They give the same rule, and each politely names the other as the important guest.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda illustrated:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן הֶסְפֵּידָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת.
phrases.english: For example, a eulogy at which Rav Sheshet is present.
phrases.notes: Because of him, crowds will come.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet illustrated:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן הֶסְפֵּידָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא.
phrases.english: For example, a eulogy at which Rav Chisda is present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what a public eulogy is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A eulogy becomes public when a great Sage attends and so the whole community comes.

steps.title: רפרם eulogizes his daughter-in-law in a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: רפרם held a eulogy for his daughter-in-law in a בית כנסת, saying everyone would come for his honor and hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם eulogized his daughter-in-law in a synagogue. He said: Because of my honor and the honor of the deceased, everyone will come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that shows the rule in action. רפרם judged that the eulogy would be public, so a בית כנסת was allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His daughter-in-law was not a Torah scholar, yet the eulogy counted as public. His own honor together with hers would bring the whole town. This shows that 'public' depends on the crowd that actually comes.

phrases.english: Rafram eulogized his daughter-in-law
in a synagogue. He said:
Because of my honor and that of the deceased
everyone will come.
phrases.notes: So it counts as a public eulogy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of a public eulogy held in a בית כנסת.
steps.raayaObject: That a eulogy which draws the whole community may be held in a בית כנסת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רפרם with his daughter-in-law.

steps.title: רבי זירא eulogizes a scholar in a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא eulogized a Sage in a בית כנסת, saying everyone would come either for his own honor or for the dead Sage's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא eulogized a certain Sage in a synagogue. He said: Either because of my honor or because of the honor of the deceased, everyone will come.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story supports the same rule. רבי זירא was sure the crowd would come, so the eulogy counted as public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רפרם needed both honors together. רבי זירא says either honor alone would be enough to draw everyone. The deceased here was a Torah scholar, so his own honor could fill the room.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the Sages, a Torah scholar

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira eulogized a certain Sage
in a synagogue. He said:
Either because of my honor,
or because of the honor of the deceased,
everyone will come.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא סַפְדֵיהּ לְהָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן בְּבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רפרם's, with a slightly different wording: either honor is enough.
steps.raayaObject: That a eulogy expected to draw everyone counts as public and may be held in a בית כנסת.
steps.whatToRemember: A הספד של רבים is one that draws the whole community, whether because of the Sage giving it or the person who died. Such a eulogy may be held in a בית כנסת.

steps.title: ריש לקיש praises a humble scholar from the back row
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש eulogized a young scholar who studied in the 24th row and declared that ארץ ישראל had lost a great man.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש eulogized a certain young Torah scholar who was often found in ארץ ישראל and who used to study הלכה in the twenty-fourth row. He said: Alas, ארץ ישראל has lost a great man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to more stories about eulogies. This one shows ריש לקיש giving high honor to a scholar who did not look important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in the 24th row meant he was far from the leading scholars. ריש לקיש still called him a great man. A person's real Torah worth matters more than his public rank.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ סַפְדֵיהּ לְהָהוּא צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: Reish Lakish eulogized a certain young Torah scholar
who was often found in Eretz Yisrael
who used to study halacha
in the twenty-fourth row. He said:
phrases.notes: Far back, meaning he was not a leading scholar.

phrases.aramaic: וַוי חָסְרָא אַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּבְרָא רַבָּה.
phrases.english: Alas, Eretz Yisrael has lost a great man.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ סַפְדֵיהּ לְהָהוּא צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where a eulogy may be held to how the Sages judged who deserved praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a humble scholar from the back rows deserves great praise in his eulogy.

steps.title: רב נחמן refuses to eulogize a 'basket of books'
steps.stepSummary: A man who memorized הלכות, ספרא, ספרי and תוספתא died. רב נחמן was asked to eulogize him and refused, asking whether he should mourn the loss of a basket full of books.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man who used to study הלכה, ספרא, ספרי and תוספתא died. They came and said to רב נחמן: Let the Master eulogize him! He said: How can I eulogize him? Should I say, 'Alas, a basket full of books is lost'?
steps.whatsHappening: This story is the opposite of the previous one. A man who knew many texts by heart was not given a eulogy by רב נחמן, because he did not truly understand what he learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A basket that holds books does not understand them; it only carries them. רב נחמן meant that this man held texts without real understanding, so there was no great scholar to praise. The next step shows that the גמרא contrasts this with ריש לקיש's generous eulogy, and it treats ריש לקיש's attitude as the more respectful one.

keyTerms.meaning: ספרא, the מדרש הלכה on ויקרא
ספרי, the מדרש הלכה on במדבר and דברים

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not mocking Torah learning. He is saying this man memorized words without understanding them, so calling him a great scholar in a eulogy would not be true.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש praised a back-row scholar as great, while רב נחמן would not praise a man who learned much but was not proficient. The next step tells us which response the גמרא admires more.

phrases.english: A certain man who used to study halacha,
Sifra, Sifrei and Tosefta, and he died.
They came and said to Rav Nachman:
Let the Master eulogize him!
He said: How can I eulogize him?
Alas, a basket full of books has been lost?!
phrases.notes: He carried texts but did not understand them, like a basket that holds books.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּהֲוָה תָּנֵי הִלְכְתָא סִיפְרָא וְסִיפְרֵי וְתוֹסֶפְתָּא וּשְׁכֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A contrasting story: the humble back-row scholar is praised, while the man who memorized without understanding is not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who memorized texts without understanding them is not eulogized as a great scholar.

steps.title: The tough scholars of Israel versus the pious scholars of Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a lesson from the two eulogy stories. The 'tough' ריש לקיש honored even a minor student, while the 'pious' רב נחמן refused to eulogize a man who knew a great deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see the difference between the tough scholars of ארץ ישראל and the pious scholars of בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to comment on the two stories it just told (steps 22 and 23) and compares them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש was famous for being harsh, yet he called a student from the 24th row 'a great man.' רב נחמן was famous for being saintly, yet he dismissed a man who had memorized הלכות, ספרא, ספרי and תוספתא as just 'a basket of books.' The point is that even the toughest scholar of ארץ ישראל showed more respect for תורה learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see. This phrase introduces an observation or lesson.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not praising the scholars of בבל. The phrase 'pious ones' sets up an ironic contrast: the 'tough' Israeli scholar actually showed more honor to a Torah learner.

phrases.english: Come and see
what the difference is between the harsh ones of the Land of Israel
and the pious ones of Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא חֲזִי מָה בֵּין תַּקִּיפֵי דְּאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל לַחֲסִידֵי דְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a comparative lesson from the two eulogy stories in steps 22 and 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even the 'harsh' ריש לקיש showed more honor to Torah learners than the 'pious' רב נחמן did.

steps.title: Using the crown of Torah: being served by one who learns הלכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה saying that one who uses the 'crown' will perish. ריש לקיש explains that this means having someone who learns הלכות serve you.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: 'One who makes use of the crown will perish.' ריש לקיש taught: this means someone who makes use of a person who studies הלכות, because הלכות are the crown of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from פרקי אבות about not using תורה for personal benefit. ריש לקיש then explains what that teaching means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's phrase 'using the crown' is vague. ריש לקיש makes it concrete: it means having a Torah learner serve you. The reason is that the הלכות such a person knows are the crown of the תורה, so using him is like using the crown itself.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
One who makes use of the crown

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that the rest of this passage deals with: a Torah scholar should not be used as a personal servant.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishna):
And one who makes use of the crown will perish.
Reish Lakish taught:
This is one who makes use of (is served by) someone who studies halachos,
which are the crown of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related theme about honoring Torah scholars. The previous steps were about eulogizing scholars; this one is about not using them as servants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being served by someone who learns הלכות counts as 'using the crown' and brings punishment.

steps.title: עולא: one who learns versus one who teaches
steps.stepSummary: עולא narrows the rule. A person may be served by someone who has learned the four orders of משנה, but not by someone who teaches them.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: A person may be served by someone who studied four orders of משנה, but should not be served by someone who teaches four orders of משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a limit to ריש לקיש's rule by separating a student of משנה from a teacher of משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being served by someone who has learned is less severe, so it is allowed, or at least it is the better choice. The real ban applies to someone who teaches others, because he is a source of תורה for others. The difference in wording between תָּנֵי (learns) and מַתְנֵי (teaches) carries the whole point.

keyTerms.meaning: To make use of someone, to be served by him

steps.confusionAlert: The two words look almost the same. תָּנֵי means 'learns' and מַתְנֵי means 'teaches.' The entire rule depends on this difference.

phrases.english: And Ulla said:
A person may be served by one who studies four (orders of the Mishnah),
but he should not be served by one who teaches four (orders).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא: לִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ אִינִישׁ בְּמַאן דְּתָנֵי אַרְבְּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows ריש לקיש's rule to apply mainly to someone who teaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may be served by someone who learned משנה, but not by someone who teaches משנה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש is carried across the water by a learned man
steps.stepSummary: A man carried ריש לקיש across a stream. When ריש לקיש learned that the man knew תנ״ך and four orders of משנה, he protested that such a person should not be carrying him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the story of ריש לקיש. He was walking on the road and came to a stream of water. A certain man came, put him on his shoulders, and began carrying him across. ריש לקיש asked him: 'Have you read Scripture?' He answered: 'I have.' 'Have you learned משנה?' 'I have learned four orders of משנה.' ריש לקיש said: 'You have carved out four mountains, and you are carrying the son of Lakish on your shoulders?! Throw the son of Lakish into the water!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about ריש לקיש to show how the rule against being served by a Torah scholar works in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש himself had taught that being served by a Torah learner is forbidden. So once he heard this man had mastered four orders of משנה, he would rather be dropped in the water than be served by him. The story shows how seriously he took his own rule. The tension it creates is resolved in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A stream or deep puddle of water
You have carved four mountains, a picture of mastering four orders of משנה

phrases.english: As in this case of Reish Lakish:
he was walking on the road
and reached a stream of water.
A certain man came,
placed him on his shoulders,
and was carrying him across.
He (Reish Lakish) said to him: Have you read (Scripture)?
He said to him: I have read.
Have you learned (Mishnah)?
I have learned four orders of Mishnah.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פְּסַלְתְּ לָךְ אַרְבְּעָה טוּרֵי
phrases.english: He said to him: You have hewn for yourself four mountains,
and you carry the son of Lakish on your shoulders?!
Throw the son of Lakish into the water!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הֲוָה אָזֵיל בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story that illustrates the rule about being served by Torah learners.
steps.raayaObject: The rule against being served by someone who has learned תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of ריש לקיש being carried across the water

steps.title: ריש לקיש's solution: become the man's teacher
steps.stepSummary: The man said he was glad to serve. ריש לקיש answered that if so, the man should first learn something from him, so that he would be serving his own teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The man said to him: 'It is my pleasure to serve the master.' ריש לקיש said: 'If so, learn this thing from me that רבי זירא said.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story's problem gets solved here. ריש לקיש finds a way to accept the man's service properly. The next step gives the actual teaching he shared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student is allowed to serve his teacher. By teaching the man something new, ריש לקיש became his rebbe, so the service was no longer 'using the crown.' It became a student honoring his teacher.
steps.whatToRemember: Being served by a Torah scholar is a problem, unless you are his teacher. A student serving his rebbe is proper and even praiseworthy.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is pleasing to me
to serve the master.
(Reish Lakish said:) If so,
learn from me this matter

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נִיחָא לִי דַּאֲשַׁמְּעֵיהּ לְמָר. אִי הָכִי, גְּמוֹר מִינִּי הָא מִלְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension from step 27 by turning ריש לקיש into the man's teacher.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once ריש לקיש taught the man, the man could properly serve him as a student serves his teacher.

steps.title: רבי זירא: Jewish women's stringency about a mustard-seed drop
steps.stepSummary: The teaching ריש לקיש shared: Jewish women took on a stringency to count שבעה נקיים even for a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי זירא said: Jewish women were strict on themselves. Even if they see a drop of blood as small as a mustard seed, they wait seven clean days because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the content of the lesson ריש לקיש taught the man, quoted from רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the letter of the law, some sightings of blood would not require seven clean days. Jewish women chose to treat even the tiniest drop with the strictest standard of זבה. The specific halacha matters less here than what it accomplished in the story: it made ריש לקיש the man's teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: A drop of blood the size of a mustard seed

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement of רבי זירא is the well-known source for the practice of counting שבעה נקיים for any blood, which is accepted הלכה.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵן הֶחֱמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן
phrases.english: The daughters of Israel were strict upon themselves
that even if they see a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed
they wait on its account seven clean days.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵן הֶחֱמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the actual teaching that ריש לקיש promised to teach in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Jewish women took on themselves to count שבעה נקיים even for a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed.

steps.title: Whoever learns הלכות is promised the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי אליהו teaches that anyone who learns הלכות is guaranteed a share in עולם הבא. The proof is the פסוק 'הליכות עולם לו', read as 'הלכות' instead of 'הליכות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of אליהו taught: Anyone who studies הלכות is guaranteed that he will have a share in עולם הבא. The פסוק says 'הליכות עולם לו', 'His ways are eternal.' Do not read it as 'הליכות' (ways). Read it as 'הלכות' (laws).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more praise of learning הלכות: whoever learns them is promised עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the earlier steps, where the 'crown' that must be honored was explained as הלכות. Here the reward for learning הלכות is spelled out, and it is proven with an 'אל תקרי' reading. The word 'הליכות' (ways) is reread as 'הלכות' (laws), so the פסוק now says that הלכות bring eternal life.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school of אליהו (תנא דבי אליהו, an early collection of teachings)
One who has a share in the World to Come
'Do not read it as…'. A method of learning a lesson by rereading a word with different vowels

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the written text of the פסוק is wrong. The simple meaning stays. The rereading adds an extra lesson on top of it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for the special importance of learning practical הלכה. The parallel version of this teaching in מסכת נדה (73a) explicitly says 'כל השונה הלכות בכל יום', anyone who learns הלכות every day. That is where the words 'every day', which some add here, come from.

phrases.english: The school of Eliyahu taught:
Anyone who studies halachos
phrases.notes: You may see 'every day' added here to explain, but those words aren't actually in the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: is guaranteed that he is destined for the World to Come,
as it is stated: "His ways are eternal"
Do not read it as "halichos" (ways)
but rather as "halachos" (laws).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of honoring those who learn הלכות (steps 25–29) by stating their reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone who learns הלכות is guaranteed עולם הבא, learned from rereading 'הליכות' as 'הלכות'.
steps.whatToRemember: Learning הלכות is so valuable that it guarantees a share in עולם הבא. This closes the section on honoring Torah learning.

steps.title: Opening a new ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new ברייתא with 'תנו רבנן'. Its content begins in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a new ברייתא, and its content comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תנו רבנן' signals that a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה, is about to be quoted. On its own it gives no ruling yet. It opens the next topic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our Rabbis taught.' This phrase introduces a ברייתא
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: The Sages taught (in a baraita):
phrases.notes: The content of this ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition. After finishing the praise of learning הלכות, the גמרא opens a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introductory formula only. The ruling follows on the next amud.
